content_of_post_to_comment: realizing I don't know why exactly geocentrism was considered an important theological point to hold at the time of Galileo and friends was it purely traditionalist inertia, or did theological frameworks of the time depend on geocentrism in important ways I suppose I'm also not entirely sure how theologically important geocentrism was to the church at the time either
comment: The interesting tension is that geocentrism was less a standalone doctrine than part of a worldview where cosmic order, human meaning, and scriptural interpretation reinforced each other. The Galileo conflict seems as much about authority over interpretation as astronomy itself.
